nodes.name: Double-confined synthesis of Ni-P nanocatalysts
nodes.procedure: Subnanometric Ni-P HCs were synthesized according to the double-confined strategy reported in our previous study. Specifically, carbon nanomaterials with abundant micropores and nitrogen dopants were used as supports to concurrently utilize the physical spatial confinement of micropores and chemical confinement of nitrogen sites. By adjustment of the calcination temperature, nickel phosphide nanocatalysts with different particle sizes were successfully synthesized. For comparison, Ni-P nanoparticles (NPs) were prepared. To investigate the role of P, subnanometric Ni clusters without P (denoted as Ni Cs) were also synthesized.

nodes.source_text: The electrochemical performance of all samples in the NO3-RR was evaluated in a standard H-type electrolysis cell by using an electrolyte containing 0.1 M KNO3 and 0.5 M Na2SO4 (pH = ~7). Figure 3a shows the linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves of Ni-P HCs, Ni-P NPs, and Ni Cs... Ni-P HCs exhibit current densities larger than those of Ni-P NPs and Ni Cs across the entire potential window... the FE of NH3 (FENH3) on Ni-P HCs shows a volcanic curve with a maximum value of 93.7% at -0.8 V versus RHE... Ni-P HCs exhibit a maximum YRNH3 of 0.61 mmol h-1 cm-2 is reached at a potential of -0.8 V versus RHE.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show Ni-P HCs uniformly dispersed clusters with average diameter ~1.1 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images of Ni-P HCs exhibit uniformly dispersed clusters with an average diameter of ∼1.1 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM and SAED show amorphous features of Ni-P HCs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image and corresponding selected area electron diffraction pattern show the amorphous features of these clusters.

nodes.characterization_summary: No discernible peaks confirming amorphous Ni-P HCs; Ni-P NPs show Ni5P4 (110) and (103) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The amorphous feature is further evidenced by the absence of discernible peaks in the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of Ni-P HCs... Ni-P NPs exhibit obvious lattice fringes with distances of 0.147 and 0.161 nm, corresponding to the (110) and (103) planes of Ni5P4.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images show bright Ni atoms (large dots) and dark P atoms (small dots) with Ni-P distance <0.3 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the HAADF-STEM image of Ni-P HCs, two distinct types of dots are observed, that is, one is large and bright, corresponding to heavy Ni atoms, and the other is small and dark, corresponding to light P atoms... the distance between Ni and P atoms in Ni-P HCs is <0.3 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p metallic peak at 853.1 eV (Ni-P HCs) vs 852.6 eV (Ni-P NPs); P 2p shifts from 129.5 eV (NPs) to 129.0 eV (HCs) indicating electron transfer Ni→P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the binding energy of the metallic Ni peak (853.1 eV) in the XPS spectrum of Ni-P HCs is higher than that in the XPS spectrum of Ni-P NPs (852.6 eV)... The peak at 129.5 eV in the P 2p XPS spectrum of Ni-P NPs negatively shifts to 129.0 eV in the P 2p XPS spectrum of Ni-P HCs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge absorption edge of Ni-P HCs between Ni foil and NiO indicating Niδ+ valence state (0<δ<2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni K-edge XANES profiles show that the absorption edge of Ni in Ni-P HCs is located between Ni and NiO, revealing the formation of Niδ+ with a valence state between 0 and 2.

properties.description: X-ray Absorption Near Edge Structure spectrum at Ni K-edge

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier-transformed Ni K-edge EXAFS fitted to Ni-P (R=1.84Å, CN=1.8) and Ni-Ni (R=2.11Å, CN=2.5); WT-EXAFS confirms both coordinations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: we fitted the peak into two contributions: the first-shell domain for Ni-P scattering with a local maximum at R=1.84Å and the second-shell domain for Ni-Ni scattering with a local maximum at R=2.11Å... Ni-P HCs had Ni-P and Ni-Ni coordination numbers of 1.8 and 2.5, respectively.

properties.description: First sharp peak indicating Ni-Ni coordination distance

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-P HCs and Ni-P NPs have similar Ni/P molar ratio of ~5/4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, both inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) and EDS indicate that Ni-P HCs and Ni-P NPs have a similar Ni/P molar ratio of ∼5/4 (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: ECSA values measured and used to normalize LSV curves; Ni-P HCs show superior intrinsic NO3-RR activity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, we tested electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) values of different electrocatalysts, and then, these values were utilized to normalize LSV curves.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Ni and P in Ni-P HCs; confirms Ni5P4 formation in Ni-P NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping images show the uniform distribution of Ni and P in Ni-P HCs (Figure S3)... EDS elemental mapping images and XRD patterns further confirm the formation of Ni5P4 NPs.
